text:
nina: opened a small TF PR to add a secondary egress route for the gpu-subnet to handle burst traffic. can someone take a look? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6172
infra-ci: plan complete — 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. full plan attached to PR.
sam: will review in ~20m :eyes:
leo: quick q — does this touch any prod NAT attachments or only route tables? want to avoid EIP collisions
nina: only adds a route in the gpu route table in us-west-2, no NAT attachment changes
maya: paste the route resource here so i can validate the next-hop/propagation
nina: sure:
```hcl
resource "aws_route" "gpu_secondary_egress" {
  route_table_id         = aws_route_table.gpu_rt.id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  nat_gateway_id         = aws_nat_gateway.gpu_burst.id
  depends_on             = [aws_nat_gateway.gpu_burst]
}
```
maya: looks ok. please add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["propagating_vgws"] }` and a one-line entry in infra/CHANGELOG.md to note the new route. avoids noisy diffs from transient route propagations
sam: pulled this into a local plan against staging, nat id matches, no surprises. Approving now. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: heads-up — canaries should run after the DB migration window. prefer after 02:00 PST. ops can schedule if you hold the merge.
deploy-bot: Canary request queued for 2024-11-06 02:30 PST. merge will be blocked until window opens.
nina: added ignore_changes and CHANGELOG line. holding merge for canary. tagging @eng-sre for ops ack
leo: thanks — tiny nit fixed. ack from me once ops confirms
eng-sre: acked, we will monitor the canary and have on-call ready. :v:
nina: will merge to canary at scheduled time and post smoke test results in this thread.
